## Audit Result

One rule, one subject, one verdict — the atom an audit is made of. Carries the `rule` by value, the `subject`, the `status`, what was `observedValue`, any `evidence`, the `finding` if the verdict was fail or partial, and an Audit Metadata stamp.

```ts
import { AuditResult } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/audit/audit-result';
@field results = linksToMany(() => AuditResult);
```

**A card rather than a field because a result is cited.** A report links it, a finding is read out of it, and next period's run compares against it. All three need it to have a URL.

**The rule is stored by value.** A result says what was judged and by which version of the rule, so editing the rule next quarter cannot retroactively change what this run concluded — the same reason `meta.sourceVersion` exists.

**Evidence sits on the pass too.** A control that passed with nothing attached is exactly what `unproven` is for, and the isolated view says so where the evidence would have been.

## Example
The two linked examples are the interesting halves of the FY26 H2 run: `sup-03-norvik-ltd` (fail, carrying finding F-2026-014) and `sup-03-acme-supply` (unproven — the status was allowed, but the rule requires evidence and none was attached). Six more results from the same run sit alongside them.

## Non-goals
Does not evaluate — Condition produces the verdict and Audit writes it. Does not roll up; the report does. Never edited after the fact: a re-run writes new results rather than rewriting these.
